This is write protection, not a mount mode. How volumes are mounted does not change. The permission applies only to the named EFI partition and the current connection. It is cleared when the disk changes, reconnects or detaches. Every other EFI partition stays protected.

The slider uses equal whole-MiB steps inside the free region. Tick marks are MiB alignment marks, thinned on large regions, not the partition-map block edges; the LBA and size fields stay authoritative.

The slider is a uniform whole-MiB scale of the selected free region, not a proportional disk map. Tick marks are MiB alignment marks; on large regions they are thinned, so only the two labelled ends are exact: the first usable aligned LBA and the last sector the right handle can select. These are the selectable span limits, not necessarily the neighbouring block edges: an unaligned region start skips a few sectors and an unaligned tail stays outside the MiB span. The left handle sets the start. The right handle sets the end. The start must stay aligned to 1 MiB. The whole range must fit inside the region. The reducer checks the values again before a write. Type the LBA and sector count directly to use an end that is not MiB-aligned. Snap to existing partition edges lives on the raw-write disk map, where those blocks are drawn.

A scheme change reinitializes the table and erases every partition. Fix backup GPT only relocates the backup header and entry array to the current disk end and recalculates checksums; it keeps every partition and needs a readable primary GPT. Restore GPT from file is a separate Diagnostics action. Both options ask for their own confirmation; changing the scheme also lists the partitions that will be erased.
Fix backup GPT keeps all partitions. Changing the scheme erases all partitions and asks for a separate confirmation.

Bigger chunks move more data per USB request and speed up large transfers, but cancellation waits longer and a failed request can lose up to one chunk of progress.
Buffer handed to the filesystem engine per call. Larger values cut per-call overhead and speed up copies, but use more RAM and make one failed call cost more progress.
Data copied between map checkpoints. Smaller intervals lose less progress after a crash or cancel but publish the map more often, which slows the backup.

Writes only the sector ranges in the map onto %1$s; the disk outside them is not changed. COPIED ranges are compared with the image and mismatches are rewritten. COPY is refused while any range is NON_TRIED. FAILED ranges are restored from image bytes (a backup usually writes zeros there). Sector size must match and the map must fit the disk; full disk geometry need not match.
Formatting uses a native filesystem engine. Cancel is not available after it starts; wait for the engine to finish. If it fails after writing, the partition may be partially formatted.

This repairs the backup GPT from the valid primary GPT. It does not format, create, delete, or rewrite partition contents. Repair is unavailable when the primary GPT is damaged or the table is ambiguous.

Bundled, USB (VTOYEFI), and server versions are shown separately. Install erases all partitions and files and formats the data partition; confirmation is required. Update rewrites boot files and keeps data files; it does not promise atomicity.

Check never writes the stick. Download keeps validated bytes app-private until app data is cleared. Pinned releases require independent archive and member SHA-256 pins. An unpinned latest release is downloaded only after a separate warning that no independent trusted SHA is available; structural validation does not prove authenticity.
No independent trusted SHA is available for this release. Archive/member structure and checksums were validated, but authenticity is not independently verified. Source: %1$s

The app fetches the official archive over HTTPS. Nothing is written to the stick; installing or updating stays a separate confirmed action.

No independent trusted SHA is available for upstream %1$s. Structural validation is incomplete. The unpinned hash is computed from the same downloaded files, not an independent trust anchor; a damaged or substituted release can make the stick unbootable. During a normal update the data partition is preserved, but the operation is not atomic; a clean install erases data. Download only if you accept this risk; writing starts only after a separate install/update confirmation.

Resume needs a matching USB serial, disk identity and geometry. Each copied range is re-read from the disk and compared with the current image data; mismatches are rewritten. Do not change the image until the operation finishes: the image is read as-is, a change can leave mixed data, and no snapshot or immutability is promised. Partial COPY is refused; FAILED sectors are written as zeros.

Restore GPT from file writes a saved primary+backup critical-sector blob onto this medium after validation. It is not the same as Fix backup GPT on the Partitions tab, which only relocates the live backup structures to the current disk end. A file name alone does not prove the blob matches this disk.
